payment_doubt_oldest_age_seconds is the age of the oldest unresolved provider round-trip. Resolution runs on every request that touches the payment and on a 1-minute sweep, so an hour means neither is converging: the provider is still silent, the attempt carries no key to replay under, or the row cannot be loaded. Money is unaccounted for until someone asks.
annotations.summary: A provider outcome has been unknown for >1h (RFC-0021 P6)

annotations.description: payment_doubt_open counts unanswered provider round-trips. A handful at any moment is normal — every timeout creates one — but a sustained double-digit backlog means the provider is unhealthy or resolution is failing in a way the age alert has not caught yet. Compare payment_provider_unknown_total (doubt created) against payment_attempt_resolution_total (doubt settled).
annotations.summary: More than 10 provider outcomes unresolved for 30m (RFC-0021 P6)

annotations.description: A provider round-trip could not be recorded. On an unknown outcome the service refuses to park without evidence, so the pre-park state stands and asserts something the provider never confirmed. Check the payments table against the provider by hand for the window in question — the automatic path did not run.
annotations.summary: The payment attempt log refused a write (RFC-0021 P6)

annotations.description: payment_doubt_sweep_failures_total counts entries the sweep skipped entirely: the payment or refund would not load, or the row carries no idempotency key to replay under. Those entries have no automatic escape and will age into PaymentDoubtStale.
annotations.summary: The doubt sweep cannot act on some worklist entries (RFC-0021 P6)

annotations.description: A reconciliation pass found at least one payment whose internal state disagrees with the provider ledger. Parked payments are excluded from the report by design — their doubt is the attempt log's worklist — so anything counted here is real drift between what we believe and what the provider holds.

{{ $value | humanize }} provider transaction(s) in 1h fell outside the requested [from, through) window. They were excluded and the watermark held (the window will be re-scanned), but a provider that ignores bounds needs investigating before the frontier can be trusted to move. Check payment logs for the excluded ids and compare with the provider's paging behaviour.
annotations.summary: the payment provider ignored its reconciliation window bounds

annotations.description: payment_reconciliation_watermark_age_seconds is how far behind now the reconciliation frontier sits, and it only moves when a pass COMPLETES. Sustained growth means passes are failing or the ticker has stopped — and while that is true, ledger-vs-provider drift is neither detected nor alerted on. Expect a healthy value under ~600s (a 5-minute settlement lag plus the 5-minute interval).
annotations.summary: Reconciliation has not completed a pass in >30m (RFC-0021 P6)

annotations.description: More than one provider round-trip every ~20s is returning no verdict at all (timeout, transport failure, 5xx). Each one parks a payment. Nothing is lost — resolution re-asks under the same key — but the customer-facing path is answering 503 and the worklist is filling. Check the provider's own health before treating this as a payment-service fault.
annotations.summary: Provider answers are going missing (RFC-0021 P6)

annotations.description: The metrics-exporter has failed to fetch system tables from {{ $labels.hostname }} for 5 minutes. The metrics-exporter cannot reach any ClickHouse replica — the OTel logs/traces store is down and edge access logs (ClickHouse-only per ADR-061) are being dropped. The collector survives this now that it owns no DDL, but its ClickHouse sink backpressures and then drops; the schema bootstrap Job would also fail until the store returns.
The Altinity operator target (job {{ $labels.job }}) has been down for 10 minutes — CHI reconciles are frozen. The running server keeps serving; config changes and self-healing stop.

Every ClickHouse* rule in this group — readonly replica, error rates, S3 errors, replication lag, Keeper session — is blind while this fires, and vmalert reports them as healthy. Check the PodMonitor selector and the `metrics` container port on the CHI before trusting any other ClickHouse alert.

annotations.description: The filesystem backing this replica is filling. MergeTree starts refusing writes near full, and the 90-day table TTL cannot outrun a sustained ingest spike on its own. annotations.summary: Node filesystem under 15% free behind ClickHouse {{ $labels.hostname }}

annotations.summary: Node filesystem under 5% free behind ClickHouse {{ $labels.hostname }}

annotations.description: Active part count is sustained above 300 — merges are not keeping up with inserts. Left alone this ends in delayed, then rejected inserts.

One partition on this replica holds more than 300 active parts for 10 minutes — the dimension parts_to_delay_insert and parts_to_throw_insert actually enforce. Today's otel.* partition is the usual culprit: small, frequent inserts outrunning merges. Delayed inserts come next, then Too many parts rejections.
annotations.summary: ClickHouse partition with too many parts ({{ $labels.replica }})

annotations.description: The daily-partitioned otel.{{ $labels.table }} table has retained more than 93 active partitions for 6 hours despite its 90-day DELETE TTL. Ingestion can remain healthy while retention, TTL merges, or object-store access is stuck; verify partition ages and TTL merge errors before forcing any materialization.
annotations.summary: ClickHouse OTel TTL is not retiring partitions ({{ $labels.table }})

annotations.description: Inserts are being slowed by the parts_to_delay_insert guard — the step before outright rejection. Watch the parts and merges panels.

The parts_to_throw_insert guard has been rejecting INSERTs on this replica for 5 minutes (Too many parts). The collector retries, then drops; ClickHouseInsertsDelayed and ClickHouseTooManyPartsPerPartition should already be firing. Merges are not keeping up — check merge failures and memory before touching the guard.

INSERT queries on this replica have been erroring for 5 minutes — telemetry rows are being refused at the door. This counter covers every cause: too many parts (see ClickHouseInsertsRejected), a readonly replica, a schema that no longer matches what the collector sends, or credentials. Break it down by error code with ClickHouseErrorMetric_* or system.query_log.

This replica is accumulating errors across every system.errors code faster than 5/s for 10 minutes. The counter is deliberately broad and includes harmless codes — a mistyped query raises UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER too — which is why this is info and not a page. Break it down by code with the ClickHouseErrorMetric_* series, or the top-N errors table on the server-engine dashboard.

This replica has been failing S3 requests for 10 minutes: the RustFS Service is unreachable, or the clickhouse-otel bucket or its credentials are wrong. Hot-window queries and INSERTs are unaffected; queries over partitions older than 7 days fail, and TTL moves and cold-part drops retry until it clears. A replica that restarts during the outage stays down on the disk access check until RustFS returns.
annotations.summary: ClickHouse cannot reach its RustFS cold tier ({{ $labels.replica }})

annotations.description: Host reconciles are erroring — the CHI may be stuck between spec and reality. Check operator logs and recent CHI changes.
The Collector's clickhouse exporter has been failing sends for 10 minutes — OTel logs/traces are not landing in the OLAP store (VictoriaLogs/VictoriaTraces keep their own copies).

Network-level Keeper exceptions on the replication path from this replica. A replica that cannot reach the quorum stops accepting writes and stops fetching parts from its peers — it drifts silently while still answering reads. Check the quorum: kubectl -n monitoring get pods -l clickhouse-keeper.altinity.com/chk=keeper.

No Keeper reports itself leader, so the quorum is gone: every ReplicatedMergeTree table becomes read-only, INSERTs fail, and replicas stop fetching parts. SELECTs keep working, which is why nothing else looks wrong. Check the pods (kubectl -n monitoring get po -l clickhouse-keeper.altinity.com/chk=keeper) and ask each one directly: echo mntr | nc 127.0.0.1 2181 — healthy is exactly one leader with zk_synced_followers 2. Do not delete Keeper PVCs; they hold the raft log.
annotations.summary: ClickHouse Keeper has no leader — replicated writes are blocked

annotations.description: The Keeper leader has fewer than two synced followers, so the 3-node quorum has lost a member. Writes still work; losing one more takes the quorum down and turns every replicated table read-only. Usually a pod or PVC problem rather than a Keeper problem — treat it as Kubernetes first. This fires alongside ClickHouseKeeperNoLeader on a total loss, by design: the pair reads the same way as the ReplicaUnreachable/AllReplicasUnreachable pair above.
annotations.summary: ClickHouse Keeper quorum degraded — no redundancy left

annotations.description: This replica has lost its ClickHouse Keeper session and can no longer accept writes or fetch parts. Reads still succeed, so the topology looks healthy from the outside while one of three copies falls behind. Check the keeper quorum first: kubectl -n monitoring get pods -l clickhouse-keeper.altinity.com/chk=keeper.

This replica's replication log trails the freshest replica by {{ $value | humanizeDuration }}. Queries the round-robin Service sends here return stale data with no error; the collector keeps writing to the others. Check system.replicas for queue_size and the oldest queue entry's last_exception — a single un-fetchable part blocks everything behind it.
annotations.summary: ClickHouse replica more than 5 minutes behind ({{ $labels.replica }})

annotations.description: This replica has had no live ClickHouse Keeper session for 2 minutes. annotations.summary: ClickHouse replica has no Keeper session ({{ $labels.replica }})

annotations.description: A part this replica needed exists on no replica, online or offline — the rows are gone and ClickHouse has stopped trying.
